findings.evidence: P2 inserts the PRIVACY.md row 'Live stuck alerts (every kit, including kits with logging off) | App memory, per class ...'. Section 5.6 labels STU_DEV->ALERTS 'stuck / stuck_resolved, every kit incl. logging off'. The plan's own Q3 says it is undecided whether logging-on kits use the same endpoint ('p7-live-stuck must not guess; the threat model shows the no-log path only as decided'). The sources are silent or limited to no-log kits. The jade-8n2.2 close reason says 'client sends only stuck/stuck_resolved there in no-log mode'. ARCHITECTURE.md line 168 and the jade-p99 description speak only of kits with logging off. Writing 'every kit' into PRIVACY.md, the privacy-promise doc that p9-privacy-doc and the consent work build from, settles an open question. That breaks INV6 and the brief's invariant ('a contradiction between sources is raised as an open question ..., not silently resolved'). It also contradicts Q3 inside the plan.
findings.fix: Change the P2 row to 'Live stuck alerts for kits with logging off' (or add 'whether logging-on kits use the same store: open, Q3'). Label the diagram edge 'stuck / stuck_resolved, logging off (logging-on path: open, Q3)'. Add an AC5 grep confirming that PRIVACY.md does not contain 'every kit'.
findings.path: plan 4.5 P2; plan 5.6 required edges; plan 8 Q3

findings.evidence: OB6 requires the diagram to show 'every place adult PII and kit-level data is stored'. The p10-backups section of docs/handoff/phases/phase-10-production-deploy.md says 'Perform a full restore onto staging and record the time taken'. The staging VM (p1-staging jade-4zw, ADR 0014) therefore holds a restored copy of the production database (users, audit_log, any kit data present at drill time), and the production backup key must be used there. The required node list (STU_DEV ... RETENTION) has only production VM, object-storage and offline subgraphs. No staging node, edge or trust boundary exists, so a store of adult PII is missing and OB6 fails.
findings.fix: Add a STAGING node or subgraph (staging VM and its PostgreSQL), with an edge BACKUP -> STAGING labelled 'restore drill (p10-backups jade-6o3): copy of production data'. Name it in section 3 as a trust boundary (staging uses its own secrets per p1-staging but receives production data during the drill). Add an RR or Q on whether staging data is wiped after the drill. Add STAGING to the AC10 node-id list.

findings.evidence: OB5 requires 'Every abuse case has a named mitigation and the phase that implements it'. AB4's ARCHITECTURE.md section 9 mitigation ('Facilitator sees duplicate joins', line 182) and AB12's bounding and rate-limiting mitigation are assigned to 'the filed bead'. Section 5.8 files that bead with `bd create ... -t task -p 2 --deps discovered-from:jade-okb`, with no parent phase epic, so it is unscheduled and has no phase (RR6 admits this). AC9 passes only because these rows also contain an unrelated 'Phase 3' or 'Phase 7' citation. p9-authz-sweep (jade-sio) must link each abuse case to a passing test, and it cannot do that for an unscheduled mitigation.
findings.fix: Either file the two beads under the phase that owns the surface: p7-class-view and p7-live-stuck are Phase 7 (epic jade-7s7), so file with --parent jade-7s7 or a dependency from that epic, and write 'Phase 7, <new id>' in AB4 and AB12. Or, if choosing a phase is Mike's call, add it as an explicit question in section 8, mark OB5 as not met for the duplicate-join and alert-store mitigations until he answers, and tighten AC9 so each named mitigation, not just each row, carries a phase.
findings.path: plan 5.5 AB4 and AB12; plan 5.8; AC9 (OB5)

findings.evidence: The asset row says 'Kit codes: plain only on the printed card and the offline packing CSV'. But p2-code-cli (docs/handoff/phases/phase-02-data-model-and-kit-codes.md) prints 'a QR that opens /redeem?code=...', and the classroom flow (ARCHITECTURE.md section 5, step 1) has facilitators scan each card's QR. The plain code therefore travels as a URL query string. It lands in the adult device's browser history. It is in the request line seen by Caddy, whose access log may be 'IP-stripped' rather than off (ARCHITECTURE.md section 4), and by app request logging. It is a potential Referer value. CLAUDE.md rule 4 says plain kit codes are never logged. The threat model is the document p9-authz-sweep walks, and as planned it never names this path, so no abuse case or mitigation (p1-observability no-code logging, p9-logs grep, p9-headers Referrer-Policy no-referrer) is tied to it.
findings.fix: Correct the asset row to list the QR redeem URL (adult device history, request URLs). Add an abuse case beyond ARCHITECTURE 9, e.g. 'Plain kit code leaking from the QR redeem URL into logs, history or Referer', with mitigations p1-observability jade-alt, p9-logs jade-ada and p9-headers jade-c42 (Phase 1/9). Add an edge PRINT -> ADULT_DEV 'QR /redeem?code=' to the diagram.
